Problem: Given that $\sin \alpha = 1 - \sqrt{3} \tan 10^\circ \sin \alpha$, find the value of the acute angle $\alpha$ in degrees.

<reflection>
Rearranging the original equation gives sin α + √3 tan 10° sin α = 1. Factoring gives sin α(1 + √3 tan 10°) = 1. Substituting tan 10° = sin 10°/cos 10° and combining gives sin α((cos 10° + √3 sin 10°)/cos 10°) = 1. Multiplying by cos 10° gives sin α(cos 10° + √3 sin 10°) = cos 10°. Using cos 10° = sin 80°, the equation becomes sin α(sin 80° + √3 sin 10°) = sin 80°, so the RHS is sin 80°, not 1.
The equation at that stage is sin α(sin 80° + √3 sin 10°) = sin 80°, so the target value is sin 80° ≈ 0.9848, not 1. Comparing the computed LHS to 1 is incorrect.
Use the corrected equation sin α(sin 80° + √3 sin 10°) = sin 80° and simplify sin 80° + √3 sin 10° using a sine addition identity to solve for α exactly.
</reflection>
